chapter: Chicago, Villa Venice and Louis Armstrong
title: The band strikes at Castle Farms in Cincinnati
summary: The musicians refuse to play until paid the full $40, Armstrong waits alone at Castle Farms, then the band breaks up back in Chicago.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: So in Cincinnati we say well, we're not going to work. We strike. We spoke to the bus driver, and he says well I got to deadhead back anyway, so anybody want to go back to Chicago is welcome to ride with us.

So when we found that out we say, 'Well look, we not working until we get all of our money.' You know. So Louis had gone on, and got dressed and gone on out to Castle Farms, and he was sitting out there by himself, and so Mike, Mike
McKendrick went out there and he related to Louie what our feelings were, and Louie sit and waited, and waited, and waited, well now they stand to be sued, you know. If you've no band.
Okay, so they agreed to pay us the $40.00. Well, they paid us the $40.00, and then after this we went on back to Chicago, and when we went back to Chicago, this is when the band broke up.
But before, Teddy Wilson had left the band, and Charlie Beal had joined the band on piano --
And Harry Dial had joined the band on drums.
